claims.claim: early-life mass-specific metabolic rates were independent or nearly independent of mass (slopes −0.45 to +0.14) (cited as abstract)
claims.note: No full text. The résumé gives the two parts separately: across the early-life literature, mass dependence 'varies strongly', with mass-specific slopes from −0.45 to 0.14; in the three species with whole-life data (carp, rainbow trout, red sea bream) early-life rates were independent or nearly independent of mass (a biphasic ontogeny). A mass-specific slope of −0.45 is far from independence, so the paper's sentence, which puts the range in brackets after 'independent', misreads it even on the abstract.

claims.claim: larval metabolism scales ~isometrically (co-cited with Oikawa et al. 1991)
claims.note: The résumé supports near-isometry for the early stages of the three species with whole-life data, not for larvae in general.
